commitResults.messageTitle: Modified programming and IDE experience to novice
Changed chtabot name from Duke to Buddy
Updated initial code to simply greet user and exit
Give Buddy ability to add and list tasks
Added the 'present-changes-visually' skill for claude code
implemented mark and unmark commands without additional classes
mark/unmark tasks, now with Task class
Buddy: extract task locals, tidy style, document main()
commitResults.messageBody:
listTasks, markTask, and unmarkTask repeatedly re-indexed
taskStorage for the same task; store it in a local `task`
variable instead so each method reads more clearly and avoids
redundant lookups. Also add the missing space before the brace
in the "mark" branch condition, per the SE-EDU Java coding
standard, and add a Javadoc comment to main() explaining Buddy's
run loop, since its behavior (read commands until "bye") is not
obvious from the signature alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tracking of Todo, Deadline, and Event task types

commitResults.messageBody:
main() mixed command parsing, dispatch, and per-branch task
construction/storage/printing in one ~40-line method, which broke the
code quality guideline of keeping methods under 30 lines and a single
level of abstraction per method. Move the switch statement into a new
handleCommand(String) helper so main() now reads as a plain
print-greeting-then-loop.

The todo/deadline/event/default branches each repeated an identical
create -> storeTask -> printBoxed sequence. Extract that into
addAndPrintTask(Task) to remove the duplication (DRY).

printMessage, printBoxed, storeTask, listTasks, markTask, and
unmarkTask were declared public static even though nothing outside
this class calls them (confirmed by searching for "Buddy." elsewhere
in the repo). Narrow them to private static to match the encapsulation
already used for this file's other helpers and keep Buddy's public
surface limited to main().

Also drops a comment on Task.getStatusIcon() that only restated the
line of code next to it.

No behavior or console output changes: the existing UI test plan
(test/ui-test-plan.md) passes unchanged after this refactor.

Add a checked BuddyException so bad input produces a message
instead of a crash or silently bad data:
- todo: reject empty description
- deadline: reject empty description; require /by
- event: reject empty description; require /from and /to
Caught once in handleCommand so the session continues after
a bad command instead of crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle mark/unmark errors and unknown commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Add task-number validation to mark/unmark, and reject unrecognized
command words, via the same BuddyException flow:

- mark/unmark: reject missing task number, non-numeric task number,
  and out-of-range task number
- unknown command: reject instead of silently adding as a task

Caught once in handleCommand, same as todo/deadline/event.

Split the previously flat src/main/java classes into packages by
responsibility, matching the SE-EDU reference layout:

- buddy: Buddy (entry point)
- buddy.task: Task, Todo, Deadline, Event
- buddy.exception: BuddyException

Update run_ui_tests.py to compile recursively and invoke
buddy.Buddy, since it assumed a flat, single-package source tree.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save and load tasks to/from disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks only lived in memory, so they were lost on every exit. Add
Storage.save()/load() to persist them to ./data/buddy.txt.

- Save the task list after every add, delete, mark, or unmark, so no
  separate save step is needed and nothing is lost on a crash.
- Load previously saved tasks on startup; start with an empty list
  if the save file doesn't exist yet, e.g. on a fresh clone.
- Skip individual corrupted lines when loading (missing fields or an
  unrecognized task type) instead of crashing the whole program.
- Add Task#toSaveFormat(), overridden per task type, to encode/decode
  the pipe-delimited save format.
- Ignore /data/ in git since it's generated runtime output.
- Reset data/ before each test-ui replay so saved state from one
  simulated session doesn't leak into the next.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Gradle build with shadowJar support
commitResults.messageBody:
Running Buddy required manually compiling with javac and tracking the
right classpath/main-class each time, and there was no way to package
it as a single distributable file.

- Add build.gradle/settings.gradle configuring the java and
  application plugins (mainClass = buddy.Buddy, Java 25 compat).
- Add the com.gradleup.shadow plugin so `./gradlew shadowJar` bundles
  everything into one runnable build/libs/buddy.jar.
- Add the Gradle wrapper (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/) so
  the project builds without Gradle installed locally.

Buddy.java directly manipulated a raw ArrayList<Task> field from six
different methods (add, get, remove, size all scattered across the
class), which is the first step toward the god-class problem the
A-CodeQuality guide's Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList target calls out.

- Add TaskList, wrapping the task ArrayList behind add/remove/get/
  size/asList operations instead of exposing it directly.
- Replace Buddy's `taskStorage` field and all its call sites with a
  `taskList` field of this new type.
- asList() exists only so Storage.save() still has a plain List<Task>
  to write out; a later Storage rework may remove the need for it.

No behavior change: all 27 test-ui cases still pass unchanged. This is
the first of several planned extractions (Ui, Parser, and an
instance-based Storage/TaskList wiring are next).

All System.out.println calls (the divider line, greeting banner, and
every confirmation/error message) move from Buddy into a new
buddy.ui.Ui class. Buddy now holds a private static Ui ui field and
calls ui.showXxx(...) instead of formatting output itself.

This is the second step (after TaskList) of the SE-EDU A-CodeQuality
extraction: separating "how to talk to the user" from "what the
command does." Buddy's command-handling methods (setTaskStatus,
deleteTask, addAndPrintTask, handleCommand, main) now only decide
*that* something should be shown and hand off the details, rather
than mixing business logic with console formatting.

No behavior change: the same 27 ui-test-plan cases pass with
byte-identical output before and after.

Command-parsing logic - stripCommandWord, and the todo/deadline/event
construction and task-index validation - moves from Buddy into a new
buddy.parser.Parser class. Buddy's createTodo/createDeadline/createEvent
become Parser.parseTodo/parseDeadline/parseEvent (renamed to match the
class's role: turning raw input into validated data, not deciding what
to do with it).

parseTaskIndex now takes the current task count as a plain int instead
of reading Buddy's taskList directly, so Parser has no dependency on
task-list state - it only checks whether a command line is
well-formed, given the info it needs to do that.

This is the third step of the SE-EDU A-CodeQuality extraction, after
TaskList and Ui. Buddy's handleCommand now reads as pure dispatch:
recognize the command word, ask Parser to make sense of the rest, act
on the result. No behavior change: the same 27 ui-test-plan cases pass
with byte-identical output before and after.

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert Buddy and Storage to instance-based design
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage gains a constructor taking the save-file path, replacing its
static FILE_PATH constant and static save/load methods with instance
fields and methods. This lets multiple Storage instances point at
different files in principle, and matches the constructor-based shape
requested by the A-CodeQuality target (new Storage(filePath)).

Buddy's taskList, ui, and storage move from static fields to instance
fields wired up in a new Buddy(String filePath) constructor. All
command-handling methods (setTaskStatus, markTask, unmarkTask,
deleteTask, addAndPrintTask, handleCommand) drop 'static' and use
these instance fields directly. The former main() body becomes an
instance method run() (greeting + input loop); main() itself shrinks
to "new Buddy("data/buddy.txt").run();", matching the target's
"new Duke(filePath).run()" shape.

This is the fourth and final structural step of the A-CodeQuality
extraction (after TaskList, Ui, Parser): Buddy no longer relies on any
shared static mutable state, so multiple independent Buddy instances
could coexist (e.g. in tests) without interfering with each other.
No behavior change: the same 27 ui-test-plan cases pass with
byte-identical output before and after.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Command classes; Parser now returns Commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds the stretch-goal Command pattern: an abstract Command class with
execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) and isExit(), and five concrete
subclasses - AddCommand, ListCommand, MarkCommand, DeleteCommand,
ExitCommand - each holding just the data it needs (e.g. AddCommand
holds the Task to add; MarkCommand holds the index and target status).

Parser.parse(String fullCommand) is now the class's only public
method, returning the Command the line represents. Parser only checks
syntax (is a task number present, is it numeric); a shared
Command.requireValidIndex(index, taskCount) helper checks whether the
number refers to an existing task at execute() time, since execute()
is the first point a Command has access to the live task list. This
also matches the target run() shape more closely, where
Parser.parse(fullCommand) takes only the raw string.

Buddy.run() shrinks to the loop from the target design: read a line,
Parser.parse it into a Command, command.execute(...) it, check
isExit(). All of Buddy's former command-handling methods
(setTaskStatus, markTask, unmarkTask, deleteTask, addAndPrintTask,
handleCommand) are gone - their logic now lives in the Command
subclasses that own it. Buddy.java is ~60 lines: a constructor wiring
dependencies, run(), and main().

Kept Ui's existing design (each showXxx method prints its own divider
lines) rather than moving line-printing into the run() loop as the
illustrative example shows - that would change every test's expected
output for no functional benefit, and the requirement explicitly
allows the design to differ from the example. No behavior change: the
same 27 ui-test-plan cases pass with byte-identical output before and
after.

Deadline stored /by as a plain String, so bad input like "Sunday"
was silently accepted. Change Deadline.by to LocalDateTime, parsed
from "yyyy-MM-dd HHmm" (e.g. 2019-12-02 1800) and displayed as
"MMM dd yyyy, h:mm a" (e.g. Dec 02 2019, 6:00 PM); bad input now
throws BuddyException.

Formatter's Locale is pinned to ENGLISH - without it, output
depended on the JVM's default locale (lowercase "pm" here).

Storage round-trips the new field; DateTimeParseException joins the
exceptions load() tolerates per corrupted line. Test plan updated
to match.
Parse deadline dates as LocalDateTime

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.find(keyword) returns tasks whose description contains it.
FindCommand and a new Parser "find" case wire this into the existing
Command pattern; a blank keyword is rejected like other commands'
missing arguments.

Ui.showMatchingTasks displays the numbered matches, or "Buddy
couldnt find any tasks with that keyword." when none match, instead
of printing an empty list.

Test plan covers a keyword with matches, no keyword, and a keyword
with no matches.
Add find command to search tasks by keyword

commitResults.messageTitle: Add trailing newline to trigger a fresh Pages build
commitResults.messageBody:
The GitHub Pages deployment was stuck serving an old commit despite
several Settings-based reset attempts (branch toggle, Source mode
switch) not registering as real changes. A push-triggered build goes
through a different code path than a settings save, so this trivial
change forces GitHub to build and deploy the current commit.

TaskList.find() didn't mention its match is case-sensitive, which
isn't obvious from the method name alone. Storage.save() described
what it does but not when it's called (after every task-list-
changing command), which explains why it exists as its own method.
Clarify find() and save() Javadoc
